evidence:
Required measured reward-discrimination evidence is absent; static shaping is supported, but a spread across actual partial-quality apps has not been established. I inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A41:E41 identifies check 40 and says 'The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing.' Internal Quality Checks!A41:Z41 repeats the check and has no additional annotation. The frozen Harbor SKILL.md Delivery profile requires shaped functional/polish/visual scoring behind gates and a functional floor; references/quality-checks.md:165-166 warns about collapsed signal from an all-or-nothing gate or common precondition. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Runtime and model evidence, requires separate hash-bound reward-discrimination runtime records and says missing infrastructure remains an evidence gap.

Static evidence: task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 has zero-weight render/constraints gates, weights 0.6/0.2/0.2, and functional floor 0.05. task/tests/tools/score.py:40-48 computes a weighted mean and rounds only the resulting reward after checking gates/floors; a positive graded spread is mathematically possible. Parsed all five judge files: 64 functional binary rows with total weight 32.7, 7 polish binary rows with total weight 4.0, and 6 visual five-point Likert rows with total weight 6.0. All scored aggregations are weighted_mean. Gates require an authored working Run and an actual shared server write/read, rather than advanced completeness (gates/render/judge.toml:25-27; gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29). Public notes require both code execution and the shared library (environment/instructions/overview.md:3-9; integration.md:7). Missing Auto-run is expressly local to its outcomes (tests/app_context.md:16; functional/prompt.md:15); ordinary failures remain local (functional/prompt.md:5,9-11,98-100; polish/prompt.md:20-22,34-39; visual/prompt.md:13-16,46-51). Fallback controls preserve partial evidence: failed uppercase/HTML dispatch does not erase lower-case/CSS facts (functional/prompt.md:S02), failed restart durability does not erase successful new writes (S22:409-415), and failed error lines/rollback do not erase recovery (S10-S13). The three Auto-run automatic/off-state rows have total functional weight 1.6, so failing those rows alone changes overall reward by approximately 0.02936 above the floor rather than zeroing the app.

Read-only scorer experiment: loaded the actual score.py through runpy and substituted in-memory suite JSON reads plus intercepted Path.write_text; no task or log files were written. With both gate inputs 1, polish=visual=0.5, functional inputs 0, 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 produced rewards 0, 0, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8. This verifies aggregation arithmetic and the strict greater-than floor only; these are synthetic dimension inputs, not measured partial-app judge rewards. The scoring policy, scorer, and test.sh are byte-identical to their frozen template copies. Thus no task-specific alteration to canonical gates, policy, or budgets is warranted from this check.

Counterexample attempts by source analysis: a fully conforming native/simple interface with proactive stale-save prevention and a static restored preview is accepted by visual/judge.toml:85, functional/prompt.md:21, and app_context.md:18; no design-specific global score collapse was found. A partial app with a dead Auto-run implementation cannot collect both off-state protection passes just by doing nothing: functional/prompt.md:379 explicitly requires observed automatic execution and says persistent failure fails both outcomes, while other observed credit survives. These are reasoned witnesses checked against the prompts, not executed app mutations.

Runtime evidence limit: raw-evidence-index.json explicitly states 'No full configured verifier, target model, Oracle or measured judge workload supplied.' Independently verified its bound RESULTS.json SHA256 ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09. That raw file identifies case='golden', browser_driver='direct pinned Playwright', paid_provider=false, oracle_score_claimed=false, and surface.visual_grade_measured=false. Its executed driver copies launch_workflow.py:phase and run_workflow.cjs:main perform scripted browser scenarios and emit product facts, not RewardKit/LLM app scores. No supplied bound artifact establishes two or more partial-app rewards through the configured scorer/judge. Scripted golden success/duration cannot establish empirical reward discrimination. Verified all 50 frozen task and 34 frozen rules file hashes against manifest.json with zero mismatches. No peer reports or previous reviewer verdicts were consulted.
suggested_fix: Provide hash-bound configured-judge runs for several deliberate partial implementations with materially different preserved features, recording per-criterion results, dimension scores and final rewards; retain the canonical harness, budgets and reward policy and reconcile any collapsed partial credit those runs reveal.
